messages:
Alex (support): Hey team, customer hitting 400 from /v1/rerank – they say it started after a client deploy. Error: \"Invalid request body: candidates must be a non-empty array\". They pasted the request body and it looks like candidates is [] sometimes or null.

Alex (support): Request id headers: X-Request-Id: req_01HJ3T2A; customer org: acme-analytics.

Alex (support): Raw payload (redacted keys):
```json
{
  \"query\": \"Which result is most relevant?\",
  \"candidates\": []
}
```

Alex (support): Also tried variant where candidates is a single object (not array) and got 400: \"candidates must be array of objects\". Customer SDK is JS wrapper v1.4.2.

Mira (eng): Thanks Alex — can you confirm Content-Type header? If requests sent with application/octet-stream or missing content-type some parsers coerce null/empty arrays.

Alex (support): They included Content-Type: application/json. Logs attached show body size ~450 bytes.

Alex (support): Full error log from our API gateway (sanitized):
```
[2026-11-03T14:23:12Z] req=req_01HJ3T2A client=54.23.12.8 POST /v1/rerank 400 validation_error candidates: path=/candidates code=ERR_REQUIRED
```

Chen (eng-ml): Quick hypothesis: client-side code might be doing JSON.stringify(obj.candidates) where candidates sometimes undefined -> becomes undefined (dropped) or null. Also some frameworks serialize empty arrays as null if not present. Could also be a shape mismatch: candidates should be [{id, text}] not {id,text}.

Jordan (sre): Any sign of spike in latency or upstream timeouts around those times? Maybe proxy truncated body leading to empty array.

Alex (support): Customer says this happens ~10% of requests after new frontend rollout. They can repro with a short repro:
1) call client.rerank(query, candidates) where candidates is derived from searchResults.map(r => r.choice) and when searchResults empty -> candidates becomes [].
2) server returns 400.

Mira (eng): Ok repro is straightforward. Two quick asks:
- Alex: ask customer to run curl example to check server behavior directly (bypass SDK).
- Customer: include X-Request-Id header from failing call and share network capture if possible.

Alex (support): Pasted curl they ran (works, returns 400):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"Which item is better?","candidates":[]}' | jq .
```

Alex (support): Response body: {"error":"Invalid request body: candidates must be a non-empty array","status":400}

Chen (eng-ml): That matches validation schema. Two action items from our side:
- Short-term: support docs + SDK should guard and surface clearer error messages. We can add client-side validation to fail early if candidates.length === 0.
- Mid-term: consider returning 422 Unprocessable Entity for semantic errors (empty arrays) to differentiate from malformed JSON. Also include error.path in response (e.g., errors:[{"path":"/candidates","message":"must be non-empty array"}]) so customers can programmatically react.

Mira (eng): I'll look into whether gateway/proxy could be stripping bodies on specific keep-alive combos. Jordan, can you check ingress logs for any anomalies around req_01HJ3T2A?

Jordan (sre): On it. Quick snippet from ingress logs shows no truncation for that request; upstream got full content-length 64 bytes. No 413/502.

Jordan (sre): Did find a cluster-level rate-limiter rule that converts 204 responses from an internal microservice to an empty array in some error path. Filing follow-up with infra.

Alex (support): Customer provided additional failing payload where candidates property is present but contains a single null: {"candidates":[null]}. API returns 400 -> \"candidate[0] must be object with id,text\".

Mira (eng): OK we should harden JSON schema validation message to include example and expected types. Will draft a small runtime change: more explicit messages and include a validation_code like VR-EMPTY-CANDIDATES. Low-risk config change to validation layer; will try to ship patch to staging.

Chen (eng-ml): Also adding a guard in reranker model adapter to skip requests that have zero candidates and return 200 with empty ranking set? That might silently hide client bugs. Better to keep 4xx but improve message.

Alex (support): Customer asks what the correct client-side check should be. Suggested snippet for them:
```js
function callRerank(query, candidates) {
  if (!Array.isArray(candidates) || candidates.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('rerank requires non-empty array of candidates');
  }
  return api.rerank({query, candidates});
}
```

Alex (support): Customer will patch frontend to validate. They've asked if we can add a server-side transitional compatibility that treats empty candidates as a no-op and returns an empty rankings array with 200 while they roll out fix.

Mira (eng): We prefer not to silently accept empty arrays. Risk: could hide logic bugs. Proposal: add a feature flag that for a short window converts the 400 into 200 with response {rankings:[]} but also log a deprecation/warning metric (metric:rerank.empty_candidates.count) and emit structured event to audit. Can gate by org id (acme-analytics) for a targeted workaround.

Chen (eng-ml): If we do that, also ensure eval pipelines ignore those and don't count as regressions.

Jordan (sre): If infra change needed we should coordinate on maintenance window. I can stand by.

Alex (support): Customer happy with that plan if we can scope it to their org for 72 hours. They requested ETA.

Mira (eng): I'll open a PR for validation message improvements and feature-flagged compatibility handler. Target: staging rollout in 48h, prod after smoke tests ~72h.

Alex (support): Filed support ticket #SUP-2026-1129 and linked the customer conversation. I'll update them with the plan and ETA. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy status: staging: validation-improve-1796 -> SUCCESS ; rollout id: r-2026-1796

Mira (eng): Staging patch looks good, added error code VR-EMPTY-CANDIDATES and example in message. Jordan, can you help schedule a canary?

Jordan (sre): Canary scheduled, will monitor metrics: 5xx, validation errors, latency. Will escalate if anything odd.

Alex (support): Closing loop with customer now. Will reopen thread if they see recurrences after the patch. Thanks all. :pray:
